findings.title: Removed validation causes delayed, confusing SyntaxError for invalid `variable` option in `_.template`
findings.description: The diff removes the only runtime validation on the `variable` option of `_.template`. Previously, if a caller passed a string containing characters like `(`, `)`, `=`, `,`, `{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, `/`, or whitespace, a descriptive `Error` was thrown immediately at template-creation time. After this change, such a value is interpolated directly into the generated function source (e.g. `function(my var) { … }`), producing a `SyntaxError` that only surfaces later when the returned template function is *invoked*. This shifts the failure from a clear, actionable error at the call site of `_.template` to a confusing `SyntaxError` at an unrelated call site of the generated function, making debugging significantly harder. Reproduction: `_.template('hello', { variable: 'my var' })` now returns a function that throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier` when called, instead of throwing `Error: Invalid 'variable' option passed into _.template` at creation time.
findings.suggestion: Restore input validation for the `variable` parameter. At minimum, check that the value is a valid JavaScript identifier (e.g. `/^[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*$/`) and throw a descriptive error if it is not. This preserves fail-fast behavior and gives callers a clear, actionable message at the point of the mistake rather than a delayed `SyntaxError`.
